app_documentation:
The Hospital Appointment Booking System, branded in the design as CareSlot, is a mobile-first web application (Web and Mobile Web) that lets patients find hospital doctors and book, reschedule and cancel appointments online. Its main purpose is to replace phone-based and walk-in scheduling with a fast, trustworthy self-service flow. A patient should be able to complete a booking in under 2 minutes. The system prevents double booking automatically and enforces a 24-hour cancellation rule. It is built with React on the front end, a Node.js REST API with JWT authentication, and a PostgreSQL database. Email goes through SMTP and SMS through Twilio.

The MVP has five features. F1, Patient Registration and Authentication, covers registration with email and phone, email verification, secure login and password reset. F2, Doctor Search and Availability, lets patients search by name, specialty or department and see open slots; doctors set weekly availability, and changes appear in the patient calendar within 1 minute. F3, Appointment Booking and Management, lets patients book, reschedule and cancel. Each slot is reserved transactionally, so no two patients can take it. F4, Notifications and Reminders, sends email and SMS confirmations within 1 minute of a booking change and a reminder 24 hours before the visit. Receptionists can see delivery status and resend failed messages. F5, Admin and Staff Management, lets administrators add, edit and deactivate doctors and departments and view appointment reports. It also lets receptionists book on behalf of patients for walk-in and phone requests.

The intended users are four roles: Patients, who register, search, book and manage appointments; Doctors, who maintain weekly availability; Receptionists, who book for patients and follow up on failed notifications; and Administrators, who manage doctors, departments, schedules and reports. The UI has six screens: Welcome and Sign In, Find a Doctor, Doctor Profile and Booking, My Appointments, Notifications and Reminders, and a role-restricted Staff Console. The design uses a teal theme with Inter typography, bottom navigation and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility. Clinical records such as diagnoses and prescriptions are out of scope; appointment notes are administrative only.

Non-functional targets are: pages load in under 2 seconds and booking requests complete in under 3 seconds at 200 concurrent users; 99.9% monthly uptime; TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest and bcrypt password hashing; HIPAA/GDPR compliance with audit logs of all patient-record access retained for 6 years. The delivery plan has 14 tasks (T1 to T14) covering database design, a design system and UI kit, the API, the screens, notification integration, admin tooling, and a final phase of end-to-end, load, accessibility and security testing plus deployment. Key risks are double booking under concurrent load, compliance scope growth, Twilio/SMTP delivery issues, infrastructure effort for uptime and performance targets, and schedule slippage on the medium-priority F4 and F5 work.

Design_v1 (CareSlot UI design: 6 screens, color scheme, typography, UI components, accessibility and responsive rules)
Database_v1 (PostgreSQL schema of 17 tables including appointments, time_slots, notifications and audit_logs, with assumptions)
CyclePlan_v1 (MVP plan with tasks T1-T14, dependencies, estimates and risk register)

glossary.Time Slot: A concrete bookable block of a doctor's time, generated from availability rules and stored in UTC. It is the unit that is reserved so that two patients cannot book the same time. Its status is open, booked or blocked.
glossary.Availability Rule: A recurring weekly window (day of week, start and end time, slot length) set by a doctor or administrator and used to generate time slots.
glossary.Double Booking Prevention: Controls that stop two patients from reserving the same slot: a unique (doctor_id, start_at) index on time slots, a partial unique index on active appointments, and a row lock inside a transaction during booking.
glossary.24-Hour Cancellation Rule: A business rule, enforced in application logic, that lets a patient cancel an appointment and release the slot only if at least 24 hours remain before the visit.
glossary.Audit Log: An append-only record of access to and changes of patient records, supporting HIPAA/GDPR compliance and retained for at least 6 years.
glossary.Delivery Status: The state of an email or SMS notification (pending, sent, delivered or failed). Receptionists use it to follow up on failures and resend messages.
